newsitem.title: FRANCE: Tunisian rights activist said freed from prison.
newsitem.headline: Tunisian rights activist said freed from prison.

text.p: A Tunisian human rights activist who was jailed for eight years earlier this year has been released by the authorities without explanation, a fellow activist living in France said on Monday.

Attorney Najib Hosni, whose case has been closely followed by international human rights groups Amnesty International and the Lawyers Committee for Human Rights, was freed on Saturday from a prison near Bizerte, northern Tunisia, Tunisian Khaled Ben M'Barek told Reuters.
M'Barek is coordinator of the Centre for Information and Documentation on Torture in Tunisia and lives in Besancon, eastern France.
Hosni wrote reports on Tunisia for international rights groups and represented many individuals he believed had been jailed in Tunisia because of their political views.
He was arrested in June 1994 on charges of falsifying a contract for a property sale.
He was convicted in January and sentenced to eight years in prison. M'Barek said Hosni had been deprived of an attorney during the trial.
M'Barek said the authorities had now granted Hosni a "conditional release" rather than a pardon, meaning that the prison sentence remained a part of his criminal record.
Officials at the Tunisian embassy in Paris had no immediate comment on the release.
